digest.component_or_area: git-fetch test suite / low-speed stall detection
propositions: Full-suite scheduler load causes git-fetch dribble tests to flake by classifying valid dribbling transfers as stalled due to delayed wake-ups reducing actual throughput below the configured rate.

The test fixture applies an artificial 2-second low-speed window uniformly to both zero-byte stall controls and above-floor negative controls, creating scheduler-sensitive false positives when libcurl aborts during extended scheduling gaps.
Cumulative bytes-owed catch-up fixes delayed wake-up drift but cannot recover after libcurl has already aborted during one uninterrupted scheduling pause exceeding the configured window.

The stable remedy splits test windows by intent: retains 2-second window only for zero-byte stall tests, uses production 10-second window for one real Git/libcurl dribble integration test, and makes pacing math deterministic via unit test.
Deterministic unit test and wrapper argv tests must prove cumulative bytes-owed calculation and low-speed configuration installation independent of scheduler behavior.
